title: Normalization factorization through an integral locally birational scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $\alpha:X\prime	o X$ be integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Suppose that for each quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$, $\alpha^{-1}U$ has finitely many irreducible components, and the induced morphism $(\alpha^{-1}U)_{\mathrm{red}}	o U_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] induces a bijection on their generic points [def-sc-generic-point] and isomorphisms of local rings at those generic points. Write $
u_X:X^
u	o X$ and $
u_{X\prime}:(X\prime)^
u	o X\prime$ for componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Then there is an isomorphism $e:X^
u\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\prime)^
u$ such that $\alpha\circ
u_{X\prime}\circ e=
u_X$. In particular $
u_{X\prime}\circ e:X^
u	o X\prime$ is the normalization morphism of $X\prime$, up to this isomorphism. No normality or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on either scheme; the empty schemes are allowed.

source.place: Tag 035Q, label lemma-normalization-normal, part (3) and its footnote allowing birationality on reductions; Tag 0CDV, label lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components, identifies the componentwise construction.

proof.text: First $X\prime$ satisfies the same finite-component condition as $X$. If $W\subseteq X\prime$ is quasi-compact open, cover it by finitely many sets $W\cap\alpha^{-1}U_j$ with $U_j$ affine open in $X$. Each $\alpha^{-1}U_j$ has finitely many irreducible components by hypothesis. An open subset of a finite union of irreducible closed subsets is the union of their nonempty intersections with that open; each such intersection is irreducible. Taking the finitely many closures in $W$ of these intersections, for all $j$, expresses $W$ as a finite union of irreducible closed subsets. Its irreducible components are the maximal members among these closures, hence are finite. This verifies the hypothesis needed for the normalization chart lemma on $X\prime$, without local Noetherianity.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), proof of (3), via the affine integral-closure construction of Tags 035P, 035O and 0CDV; integrality transitivity is algebra.tex Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive).

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$. Integrality of $\alpha$ means that $V=\alpha^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine and $A\to B$ is integral. Reduction has the same underlying points and residue fields: nilpotents map to zero in every residue field. By the hypothesis on the reduced generic local rings, the induced maps $\kappa_X(\eta)\to\kappa_{X\prime}(\eta\prime)$ are isomorphisms for the specified bijection of generic points in $U$ and $V$. Indeed a local-ring isomorphism identifies maximal ideals and hence their residue quotients. These are the actual residue-field maps induced by $\alpha$. Thus the finite products $C_U=\prod_\eta\kappa_X(\eta)$ and $C_V=\prod_{\eta\prime}\kappa_{X\prime}(\eta\prime)$ have an induced isomorphism $\varphi_U:C_U\xrightarrow{\sim}C_V$. It carries the structural map $A\to C_U$ to the composite $A\to B\to C_V$. Neither $A\to B$ nor $B\to C$ needs to be injective.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), proof of (3), via the affine integral-closure construction of Tags 035P, 035O and 0CDV; integrality transitivity is algebra.tex Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive).

proof.text: Let $D_A\subseteq C_U$ and $D_B\subseteq C_V$ be the integral closures of $A$ and $B$. We prove $\varphi_U(D_A)=D_B$. If $d\in D_A$, apply $A\to B$ to its monic equation; compatibility in step 2 shows that $\varphi_U(d)$ satisfies this equation over $B$, hence lies in $D_B$. Conversely take $c\in D_B$ and let $E\subseteq C_V$ be the subring generated by the image of $B$ and $c$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], the elements integral over $B$ form a subring containing these generators, so $E$ is integral over $B$. The maps $A\to B\to E$ satisfy both hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive], so $c$ is integral over $A$. Apply $\varphi_U^{-1}$ to its monic equation. Compatibility in step 2 gives a monic equation for $\varphi_U^{-1}(c)$ over the original map $A\to C_U$, proving membership in $D_A$. Neither structural map need be injective; the argument also permits the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), proof of (3), via the affine integral-closure construction of Tags 035P, 035O and 0CDV; integrality transitivity is algebra.tex Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts] to $T=X$ and $T=X\prime$, using step 1 for the latter. It identifies $
u_X^{-1}U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D_A$ and $
u_{X\prime}^{-1}V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D_B$. Step 3 gives inverse ring isomorphisms $\varphi_U|_{D_A}:D_A	o D_B$ and $\varphi_U^{-1}|_{D_B}:D_B	o D_A$. Contravariant Spec applied to the latter gives $e_U:
u_X^{-1}U\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_{X\prime}^{-1}V$, with inverse induced by the former. The composite $A	o B	o D_B	o D_A$ equals the structural map $A	o D_A$ by step 2. Thus $\alpha
u_{X\prime}e_U=
u_X$ on this open.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), proof of (3), via the affine integral-closure construction of Tags 035P, 035O and 0CDV; integrality transitivity is algebra.tex Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive).

proof.text:
The structural equation in step 4 identifies $e_U^{-1}(
u_{X\prime}^{-1}(\alpha^{-1}W))$ with $
u_X^{-1}W$ for every affine $W\subseteq U$; the inverse isomorphism has the corresponding property. Thus both directions restrict to the covering opens used below. These local isomorphisms agree on overlaps. To check $e_U$ and $e_{U\prime}$ on their common domain, cover $U\cap U\prime$ by affine opens $W$; their inverse images under $\alpha$ are affine. The restriction clause of [lem-sfb-normalization-generic-residue-affine-charts] identifies restriction on normalization sections with projection onto the generic residue fields belonging to $W$. Writing $p_X:C_U	o C_W$ and $p_{X\prime}:C_V	o C_{\alpha^{-1}W}$ for these projections, one has $p_{X\prime}\varphi_U=\varphi_Wp_X$ factor by factor. Hence also $p_X\varphi_U^{-1}=\varphi_W^{-1}p_{X\prime}$. Both ring maps restricted over $W$ are therefore $\varphi_W^{-1}|_{D_{\alpha^{-1}W}}$; equality is detected after inclusion into $C_W$ because $D_W$ is a subring. Thus the scheme maps agree on every such open. Glue the maps $e_U$ and their inverses on these open covers. The glued composites are identities because they are identities on each covering open, giving an isomorphism $e:X^
u\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\prime)^
u$. The equalities $\alpha
u_{X\prime}e_U=
u_X$ also glue, giving the required equation globally. Finally $
u_{X\prime}e$ is the componentwise normalization map of $X\prime$ transported along this isomorphism, which proves the last assertion. When $X$ is empty, a morphism $X\prime	o X$ forces $X\prime$ empty, and the same gluing over the empty cover gives the unique empty isomorphism.

lean.note: The helper Hom.reducedRestriction constructs the canonical map on reductions of the open restriction using Hom.liftNilradical; no choice of an arbitrary map is a hypothesis. The isomorphism witness identifies the factor map with the normalization of the source transported along that isomorphism.
